FF&E schedule template

The FF&E schedule is the room-by-room register of selected items. Its job is coordination: what belongs where, how many are proposed, and which information is still needed before an order can be considered.

What each field records

Room
Use a stable room name or number.
Reference
Match the plan and product specification.
Item
Describe the proposed selection.
Quantity
Count items; do not confuse a set with individual units.
Unit
Use an explicit purchasing unit.
Specification reference
Point to the current product specification.
Approval
Track selection approval separately from an order.
Order / delivery
Record actual order status only when confirmed.
Review note
Identify missing model, access, or suitability information.

How to use this template

Agree the classification boundary with your team. In this library, furniture and the loose rug sit in this register; the retained floor belongs in the finish schedule and built-in joinery stays linked to its drawing and specification. This is a documentation convention, not a universal accounting rule. Reconcile each stable reference against the plan once, then check its specification and purchasing unit before sharing.

  1. List items by room and stable reference.
  2. Reconcile quantities with the furnished plan.
  3. Confirm specification, approval, purchasing responsibility, and delivery constraints before ordering.

Reconcile quantities without double counting

Count an item once in its room register even when it appears in a plan, elevation, and presentation. Those views are references to the selection, not additional purchases. If one reference covers several instances, make the quantity and unit explicit.

The template does not generate orders or check stock. Keep the Approval column specific about the decision it records, and use Order / delivery only for supported purchasing facts. A selection may be visually accepted while product information is still being reviewed.

Review before use

  • Do not count one item again merely because it appears on two drawings.
  • Selection approval and order confirmation are different states.
  • Do not use a partial sample register as a complete purchasing list.

Units, source information, and US use

The worked example keeps its original nominal metric dimensions. For a US project, choose and label a primary imperial or metric convention, distinguish item counts from areas, and document any display conversion and rounding. Never relabel metric values as imperial or treat conversion as site verification.
